details.description: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, with 2.4 trillion total parameters and 95 billion activated per token across 512 experts (10 routed plus 1 shared), per its Hugging Face model card. It is the first time Alibaba has given a Qwen "Max"-class model an open release, built for coding, professional work, research and long-horizon agentic tasks. The checkpoint is text-only and always reasons in a "thinking" mode that cannot be disabled; Alibaba's separate commercial Qwen3.8-Max product adds vision input and a non-thinking mode on top of this checkpoint, per the model card.
advantages: Scores 92.6 on GPQA Diamond, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 67.7 on SWE-bench Pro, a real-world software-engineering benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 86.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, an agentic terminal-coding benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: Requires thinking mode for all interactions and cannot run in a non-thinking mode, per its Hugging Face model card.
The open checkpoint itself has no vision input; Alibaba's separately hosted Qwen3.8-Max product adds vision input, per the model card.
Distributed under Alibaba's own "qwen3.8-max" model license rather than a standard permissive open-source license, per its Hugging Face license tag.
use_cases: Complex, multi-step coding and software-engineering tasks
Long-horizon agentic workflows requiring autonomous planning and tool use
Professional and research tasks needing extended step-by-step reasoning

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (1,010,000) matches the model card's extended-context figure beyond its native 262,144-token window; catalog's text-only modality matches this checkpoint (Alibaba's separately hosted Qwen3.8-Max product, not this checkpoint, adds vision). No explicit language list was found on the model card. Together AI's serverless-models documentation lists this model with function calling and structured outputs both marked unsupported (dash), contradicting an earlier claim that Together supports them; that claim was removed. The GPQA Diamond/SWE-bench Pro/Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores are given on this model's own Hugging Face card, but the results table itself is headed "Qwen3.8-Max" -- the card describes Qwen3.8-Max as "the official version based on Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B with more features, such as vision input & non-thinking support" -- so the scores may reflect that served product rather than a separately-measured run of this exact checkpoint; kept because the benchmarks are text/agentic tasks unaffected by Max's added vision/non-thinking features and no other source gives different numbers, but flagging the naming for a future check.
